title: Manifest
description: A Project's identity, in a committed file. Generated by `project new`, read by the Project's workflows, by the contract check, and by anyone who opens it (ADR-0010).

$schema.description: Optional. Points an editor at this file; the checker reads the schema from its own checkout, not from the network.

slug.description: The Project's name everywhere a machine reads it: the Compose project name, the Traefik router and service names, the directory on the host, the image repository. Lower case, digits and hyphens. A leading digit is allowed, because a real Project has one and Compose accepts it.

appName.description: The Project's name where a person reads it.

appHost.description: The public hostname. Read at image-build time as well as at deploy time - the frontend bundle is compiled against it - so changing it means republishing, not redeploying.

profile.description: The Template this Project was copied from. A closed list on purpose: the contract names no language, and a Profile is the one place a language is allowed to appear, so adding one is a contract version bump rather than a free-text field.

addons.description: Optional capabilities this Project declares rather than a stack it inherits. Shared files stay byte-identical across every Project of a Profile and enable the behaviour conditionally, which is what keeps drift from the Template measurable.

contractVersion.description: The major version of the Platform Contract this Project is held to, matching the tag its workflow pins and the version its CONTRACT.md carries.

seedCommand.description: The command a Preview runs to fill an empty database with synthetic data. Required when the database Add-on is declared. Preview data is never a copy of production - that is what keeps a Preview and its testers outside production's Trust Domain.

then.description: a Project declaring the database Add-on must declare the seed command a Preview will run
